sam: quick heads-up — after the kv pager merge change merged yesterday I'm seeing a 15% P95 latency bump on continuous batching for long-context workloads. dashboard: https://dash.internal/reports/contbatch-p95

ria: ugh. can you repro locally? any flamegraphs or profiles?

sam: repro is easy with the long-context perf harness. running: `./perf/run_contbatch --tokens=8192 --qps=50 --model=redwood-1-large`

sam: pasted a small stack sample from perf recorder (trimmed):
```
KVPager::handle_page_fault  34%
BatchMerger::wait_on_page  22%
ServingRuntime::emit_tokens  18%
Scheduler::steal_work        12%
Other                      14%
```

ada: interesting — our eviction counters spike at the same time. saw kv.evictions go from ~1200/min -> ~5400/min when cont-batch merges are enabled.

michael: that suggests fragmentation + racing evictions. merged batches extend KV residency and prevent cheap reclamation, then the pager thrashes and blocks head-of-line.

sam: also seeing steady memory growth on a single connection with repeated long prompts. looks like pages not recycled between merges. not sure if it's a hole in the reuse path or a retention bug.

perf-bot: regression-detected: contbatch-kvpager-merge | p95 +15% | CI build 5823 | link: https://ci.internal/build/5823 

ria: can you dump per-batch kv-hit/hotness and page-fault rates? I want to confirm if warm caches get demoted incorrectly on merge.

ada: will grab counters. quick grep from production metrics: `kv.cache_hits/second`, `kv.page_faults/second`, `kv.fragmentation_ratio`. pattern is: when merge occurs -> page_faults spike -> fragmentation_ratio climbs 0.18 -> 0.42

michael: possible mitigation: delay merging until all batch members have warm KV fingerprints or cap merged batch size to avoid head-of-line. also consider yielding the merge lock if pager queue depth > X.

sam: i'm going to try a canary patch that disables eager merge and instead does opportunistic merge only when kv_hit_rate > 80%.

ria: if you push a branch, i'll run it against the perf harness and capture p95 + memory timeline.

ada: quick config snippet to test (in case useful):
```json
{
  "cont_batch": {
    "merge_policy": "opportunistic",
    "merge_min_kv_hit": 0.8,
    "merge_max_members": 8,
    "pager_yield_threshold": 64
  }
}
```

michael: for the repro i'll also instrument KV allocator to log fragment maps every 5s so we can see growth pattern.

sam: thanks — can we aim for a short postmortem thread after we get measurements? want to capture whether it's behavioral (policy) or bug (reuse path).

ria: +1. I'll prepare a short perf runbook: commands, metrics to collect, flamegraphs to capture, and a minimal reproducer.

ada: FYI i found one trace where eviction removed page N while merged batch still had a stale pointer to it — could be a stale ref-count path. attaching a short excerpt: `ptr=0x7ffd.. removed while refcount=1` — looks like a bug, not just a policy.

sam: that would explain memory growth + fragmentation. ok, let's triage both lanes: rollback-policy and fix-reuse. michael/ria — coordinate on runs, ada/sam on logs and heap dumps.

michael: i'll start the instrumented run in ~15m and post results here.

perf-bot: scheduled perf-run: contbatch-repro-1918765432 | started | runner: perf-03

sam: thanks everyone :thumbsup:
